extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.use_case: This application serves as an AI customer service system for an airline, handling tasks such as FAQ question answering, request triage and routing, flight status lookups, seat bookings, and cancellations. It is powered by five specialized OpenAI Agents (gpt-4.1-mini) with seven tool integrations and two guardrails (jailbreak and relevance) to ensure safe and relevant responses. The system operates solely in text mode and does not support voice, image, or video inputs.
summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider / runtime:** Azure via GitHub Actions on ubuntu-latest runners
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** Deployment targets Azure but lacks any specified regions or availability zones for resilience.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret stores:** GitHub Actions secrets (github_actions_secret)
- **Credential handling:** Azure Credentials referenced as `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` — a secret reference, not plaintext
- **Assessment:** Secret is stored in GitHub Actions secrets, which is a reasonable approach, but no encryption-at-rest or key management details are evidenced.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** Not evidenced (encryption_at_rest_coverage is false)
- **Key management:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** Encryption configuration is absent from the provided infrastructure data.

### 4) IAM / least privilege
- **Principals / service accounts:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` (managed identity)
- **Scope / permissions / trust:** Scope is subscription-level; trust principals include github-actions; IAM type is managed_identity
- **Assessment:** Subscription-wide scope grants excessive permissions, and lack of OIDC means credentials are long-lived secrets rather than short-lived tokens.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runners / triggers:** Ubuntu-latest runners; triggers include push and workflow_dispatch
- **OIDC / credential flow:** Not using OIDC (uses_oidc: false) — credential flow relies on static secrets stored in GitHub
- **Assessment:** Missing OIDC increases risk of credential exposure; static subscription-level secrets should be replaced with OIDC-based federated identity.

### 6) Container security
- **Images / root user:** Not evidenced
- **Health checks / resource limits:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No container configuration data is present in the detected infrastructure nodes.

### 7) Top 3 prioritized actions
1. Replace static `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` with OIDC-based federated identity for GitHub Actions to Azure to eliminate long-lived credential exposure.
2. Reduce the IAM scope from subscription to a resource group or specific resource level to follow least-privilege principles.
3. Enable encryption at rest and document key management (e.g., Azure Key Vault) for any data services used by the AI application.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Architecture & Data Flow**: User requests hit FastAPI endpoints (`Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, `Chat Endpoint`). The `Chat Endpoint` is protected by Bearer Auth. The `OpenAI Agents` framework orchestrates five agents (`Triage`, `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`). `Triage Agent` delegates to `Flight Status Agent` and `FAQ Agent`. All agents use `gpt-4.1-mini` and can call the same set of tools: `Baggage Tool`, `Cancel Flight`, `Display Seat Map`, `Faq Lookup Tool`, `Flight Status Tool`. Two guardrails (`Relevance`, `Jailbreak`) also use `gpt-4.1-mini` but no agent explicitly invokes them.

- **Security Observations**: 
    - **Unguarded tools**: No guardrails are enforced on any agent-tool calls. Every agent can call every tool, including `Cancel Flight` and `Flight Status Tool`, without relevance or jailbreak checks.
    - **Missing guardrail coverage**: Guardrails are isolated—they only use the LLM but are not wired into the chat endpoint or agent execution flow.
    - **No datastore exposure**: `Sqlite` is listed as a datastore but has no connections, so no data ingress/egress is visible.
    - **Broad tool access**: All agents share five tools, creating risk of unintended actions (e.g., a FAQ agent calling `Cancel Flight`).
